newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Singapore government bonds close slightly lower.
newsitem.headline: Singapore government bonds close slightly lower.

text.p: Singapore government bonds closed slightly lower in moderate trade on retail and interbank interest, dealers said on Friday.
"Bond prices were marked down slightly today following a mild hike in the interbank rate. Treasury bill yields were slightly higher. Volume was moderate," a local dealer said.
Among bonds, July 1998 ended at S$97.93/97.98 compared with Thursday's close of S$98.00/98.05, September 2001 at S$96.85/96.90 against S$96.95/97.00 and June 2003 at S$94.83/94.88 from S$94.95/95.00.
The overnight interbank offered rate rose to 2-11/16 2-9/16 percent versus Thursday's 2-5/16 2-3/16 percent.
In treasury bills, three-months closed at a yield of 2.26/2.21 percent against Thursday's yield of 2.15/2.10 percent and one-year at a yield of 2.38/2.33 percent from 2.30/2.25 percent.
